newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Britain's trade gap widens in September. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Britain's trade gap widens in September. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to make clear trade gap widened rather than narrowed; also corrects August figure in first paragraph.)
Britain's trade deficit with the rest of the world widened in September to 899 million pounds ($1.50 billion) from 568 million pounds in August, the Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday.

More up-to-date but incomplete figures covering trade with countries outside the European Union showed the improvement in trade continued in October. The trade deficit between Britain and non-EU countries narrowed to 424 million pounds from 805 million pounds in September.
The government welcomed the figures. "As the Chancellor said in his speech yesterday, exports are performing very well. The latest data confirm this," said a Treasury spokesman.
Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke unveiled his budget on Tuesday and said Britain had this year recorded its best overall trading performance for nearly 10 years.
The ONS said the trend in global trade was narrowing. ($1=.5990 Pound)
